feature: Import policy covers files declared in its layer
description: A [[import_policy]] whose layer names a hex layer also judges every file analyze.layers declares in that layer, and nothing else changes.

specs.description: A Go file declared domain by analyze.layers is held to the domain policy
specs.given: A Go project whose .hexa/project.json has analyze.layers {"perfpayload": "domain"}, and a rules file with an [[import_policy]] layer = "/domain/" whose deny list includes "os/exec" at severity "error". domain/access_control.go and perfpayload/encode.go each contain `import _ "os/exec"`
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: The policy reports one finding in domain/access_control.go and one in perfpayload/encode.go, each naming "os/exec" at its line

specs.description: A Python domain declared only by map is checked by the domain policy
specs.given: A Python project with analyze.layers {"sdk/core": "domain"} and no folder named domain. The domain [[import_policy]] (layer "/domain/") denies os, ssl and subprocess at severity error. sdk/core/client.py imports os, ssl and subprocess
specs.then: Three error findings are reported for sdk/core/client.py, and the health score is 30 points lower than for the same tree with those three imports removed

specs.description: A layer name with a slash in it, written with or without surrounding slashes, picks up its declared files
specs.given: analyze.layers {"src/db": "adapters/secondary"}, and an [[import_policy]] with layer "adapters/secondary/" that denies "net/http". src/db/store.go imports "net/http"
specs.then: A finding is reported for src/db/store.go. The same finding is reported when the policy's layer is written "/adapters/secondary" or "adapters/secondary"

specs.description: A key naming a source file also covers its module
specs.given: analyze.layers {"src/model.py": "domain"}, and a domain policy (layer "/domain/") denying subprocess. src/model/history.py imports subprocess
specs.then: A finding is reported for src/model/history.py

specs.description: A file declared in a different layer is not added to the policy
specs.given: analyze.layers {"src/http": "adapters/primary"}, and a domain policy (layer "/domain/") denying os. src/http/server.py imports os, and no segment of its path is "domain"
specs.then: The domain policy reports nothing for src/http/server.py

specs.description: A policy layer that only contains a layer name, without being exactly one, adds no declared files
specs.given: analyze.layers {"perfpayload": "domain"}, and an [[import_policy]] with layer "/domain/models/" that denies "os/exec". perfpayload/encode.go imports "os/exec"
specs.then: That policy reports nothing for perfpayload/encode.go

specs.description: Every declared file is in scope of the policy for its declared layer
specs.given: Any project and any analyze.layers map, and any policy whose layer, with its leading and trailing '/' trimmed, equals a layer name L
specs.then: The set of files the policy judges is the files its path matches, together with every file an analyze.layers key assigns to L, less the files §3 excludes. The policy judges no file outside that set

specs.description: Without analyze.layers, a policy judges exactly the files its path matches
specs.given: A project with no analyze.layers in .hexa/project.json. A domain policy denies std::fs. src/domain/a.rs uses std::fs, and src/core/b.rs uses std::fs
specs.then: The findings are the same as before this ADR: one for src/domain/a.rs and none for src/core/b.rs

specs.description: A crate named for its layer adds nothing to the policy
specs.given: No analyze.layers. A crate directory app-domain/ whose files the built-in classification grades as domain, though no path segment is "domain". A domain policy (layer "/domain/") denies std::fs, and app-domain/src/lib.rs uses std::fs
specs.then: The domain policy reports nothing for app-domain/src/lib.rs

specs.description: A key covers whole path segments only
specs.given: analyze.layers {"src/core": "domain"}, and a domain policy denying os. src/core_utils/io.py imports os
specs.then: The domain policy reports nothing for src/core_utils/io.py

specs.given: Any project with no analyze.layers, and any set of import policies
specs.then: Every import-policy finding, and the grade, are identical to what path matching alone produces

specs.description: A file matched by path and also declared is judged once
specs.given: analyze.layers {"src/domain": "domain"}, and a domain policy (layer "/domain/") denying os at severity error. src/domain/x.py imports os once
specs.then: Exactly one finding is reported for that import, and the score falls by 10 points, not 20

specs.description: Allow and severity apply to declared files as written
specs.given: analyze.layers {"pkg/model": "domain"}. A domain policy allows only "fmt" and is at severity "warning". pkg/model/a.go imports "fmt" and "net"
specs.then: There is no finding for "fmt". There is one warning for "net", and the health score is unchanged by it

specs.description: A declared file under top-level tests/ stays out of scope
specs.given: analyze.layers {"tests/fixtures": "domain"}, and a domain policy denying subprocess. tests/fixtures/run.py imports subprocess. The same holds for benches/ and examples/
specs.then: The domain policy reports nothing for files under the top-level tests/, benches/ or examples/

specs.description: Each import is judged at most once per policy
specs.given: Any project, any policy, and any file that is both path-matched and declared in the policy's layer
specs.then: Each import or reference in that file yields at most one finding from that policy. No file under a top-level tests/, benches/ or examples/ yields any

specs.description: A path policy that names no layer stays path-only
specs.given: analyze.layers {"netbox_plugin/utilities": "domain", "netbox_plugin/core": "domain"}, and a policy with layer "netbox_plugin/utilities" that denies requests. netbox_plugin/utilities/a.py and netbox_plugin/core/b.py both import requests
specs.then: That policy reports a.py and does not report b.py

specs.description: Boundary rules and the grade formula do not change
specs.given: A project whose boundary violations, cycles, dead exports and unused ports are known, and with no policy whose layer names a layer
specs.when: hexa analyze runs before and after this change
specs.then: The boundary violations and every other rule kind's findings are identical, and the health score is identical

specs.description: Non-layer policies are unaffected by any analyze.layers map
specs.given: Any project, any analyze.layers map, and any policy whose trimmed layer is not a layer name
specs.then: The policy's findings equal those produced by path matching alone. Every non-policy finding is the same as when the policy is judged by path alone

amendments.reason: Fixture defects, plus one corrected example: the rules were written to .hexa/rules.toml, which hexa never reads (it reads .hexa/ADR-rules.toml), and each [[import_policy]] lacked the required adr, id and message fields, so no policy ran and the control cases failed too; S13 used the standard-library net as the import the allow list omits, but the standard library is permitted unless denied (before and after this ADR), so it now uses an external import, example.com/ext, which keeps S13's point (allow and severity apply to declared files). Without the fix 9 fail and 8 guards pass; with it 17 pass
